solutions.explanation:
Both sine and cosine are at most \(1\). Their sum can equal \(2\) only if both terms equal \(1\), so
\[
\cos(2A-B)=1,
\qquad
\sin(A+B)=1.
\]
The triangle's interior angles are positive and sum to \(180^\circ\), so \(0^\circ<A+B<180^\circ\). In this interval, sine equals \(1\) only at \(90^\circ\). Hence
\[
A+B=90^\circ,
\qquad C=90^\circ.
\]
Now \(B=90^\circ-A\) and \(0^\circ<A<90^\circ\), giving
\[
-90^\circ<2A-B=3A-90^\circ<180^\circ.
\]
Cosine equals \(1\) at integer multiples of \(360^\circ\). The only such angle in this interval is \(0^\circ\), so \(2A-B=0^\circ\), or \(B=2A\). Combining this with \(A+B=90^\circ\) gives \(A=30^\circ\) and \(B=60^\circ\).

Side \(AB\) is opposite the right angle, so it is the hypotenuse. Side \(BC\) is opposite the \(30^\circ\) angle and therefore equals half the hypotenuse. Thus
\[
BC=\frac{AB}{2}=\frac42=2,
\]
choice C.
